items.title: Selected stationary thermal equilibrium
items.physical_scope: One selected comoving bath on a connected smooth Lorentzian domain with a future timelike Killing field and a Killing inverse-temperature vector; no universal equilibrium existence, KMS state, or empirical thermometer law.
items.design_state: Authored draft for the reserved selected stationary thermal-equilibrium claim; exact hypotheses and source dispositions are recorded in batch-66 notes.
items.statement:
On a nonempty connected open set $O$ in the smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-tgr-framework-units]], select one smooth future timelike Killing field $\xi$ and one smooth scalar $T:O\to(0,\infty)$ in kelvins. Its dimensionless lapse and selected observer congruence are

$$N_\xi:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0,\qquad u:=\xi/N_\xi.$$

Thus $g(u,u)=-1$ and the physical four-velocity is $cu$ in the length-coordinate convention $x^0=ct$. A reference normalization of $\xi$ is part of the selected model. The local temperature $T$ is assigned to this comoving observer congruence; it is not a coordinate temperature or a value assigned to every observer.

Adopt the inverse-temperature vector

$$\beta:=\frac{u}{k_BT},$$

where $k_B>0$ is Boltzmann's constant in joules per kelvin, and assume that this field is Killing on $O$. In this item, a selected stationary thermal equilibrium means precisely this adopted bath, observer congruence, positive proper-temperature field, and Killing condition on $\beta$. The field $N_\xi T$ is not assumed constant here; its constancy is the conclusion of [[pthm-tgr-tolman-ehrenfest]].

This is a model assumption, not a statement that every stationary geometry admits a thermal state or that every material realizes this bath. It asserts no complete Killing flow, KMS state, trace-class stress exponential, collision or thermalization law, Hawking or Unruh temperature, or empirical thermometer reading.

items.title: Conditional Tolman–Ehrenfest relation
items.physical_scope: Conditional redshift law for the local proper temperature of one selected connected stationary bath; no claim that arbitrary stationary flows or geometries are in equilibrium.
items.design_state: Authored draft for the reserved selected stationary thermal-equilibrium claim; exact hypotheses and source dispositions are recorded in batch-66 notes.
items.statement:
Use the connected stationary thermal carrier of [[post-tgr-stationary-equilibrium]] on $O$. Let $N_\xi=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$, $u=\xi/N_\xi$, and $\beta=u/(k_BT)$ as there, and assume the postulated Killing condition on $\beta$. Then a positive constant $T_K$ exists such that

$N_\xi(x)T(x)=T_K\quad\text{and}\quad \beta=\frac{\xi}{k_BT_K}\qquad(x\in O).$

In the same convention, $\xi(N_\xi)=0$, the observer acceleration satisfies $a=\nabla\log N_\xi$, the expansion and shear vanish, and

$\nabla\log T=-a.$

For any chosen reference event $x_{\rm ref}\in O$, $T_K=N_\xi(x_{\rm ref})T(x_{\rm ref})$. If the reference normalization has $N_\xi(x_{\rm ref})=1$, then $T_K$ is the local temperature at that event. Rescaling $\xi$ by a constant $b>0$ rescales $N_\xi$ and $T_K$ by $b$ while leaving the local scalar $T$ unchanged. The result is a conditional deduction from the selected physical postulate and the stated mathematical supplier; it is not a thermometer law for arbitrary observers or a KMS-existence theorem.

items.title: Specified equilibrium particle exchange
items.physical_scope: A selected fixed-composition local material branch with either a finite independent-cell exchange model or a massive classical charged Liouville ansatz; charged conclusions require the stated global potential symmetry and reference.
items.design_state: Authored draft for the reserved selected stationary thermal-equilibrium claim; exact hypotheses and source dispositions are recorded in batch-66 notes.
items.statement:
For a selected fixed-composition material branch, adopt the local state function and energy convention of [[post-tgr-local-material-thermodynamics]] and [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. In that state map, $T>0$ is the derivative of the supplied energy per marker with respect to entropy per marker, and the chemical potential is $\mu=H-T\sigma_p$ in joules per marker. Rest energy stays in the energy convention used for $\mu$ and for any particle generator; a rest-energy subtraction made in a different convention must be tracked explicitly.

For particle exchange, select and declare one of these physical model protocols:

- **Finite-cell exchange.** Supply $r\ge1$ finitely many independent cells with differentiable concave entropy functions $S_i(E_i,n_i)$, positive lapse values $N_i$, a fixed common charge $q$, and potential values $\Phi_i$ in a stated common reference. The adopted exchange conserves $\sum_i(N_iE_i+q\Phi_i n_i)$ and $\sum_i n_i$. The local $T_i$ and $\mu_i$ for this protocol are those defined by the entropy derivatives in [[thm-tgr-finite-entropy-exchange-equilibrium]]. Their identification with another material state map is an additional model identification, not inferred here.

- **Charged kinetic exchange.** On the selected stationary domain, supply a species of rest mass $m>0$, charge $q$, smooth local fields $T>0$ and $\mu$, a global smooth real potential $A$ with $F=dA$, and a smooth compensator $\Lambda_\xi$ satisfying $\mathcal L_\xi A=d\Lambda_\xi$. Use the future massive shell, charged transport, and dimensionless exponential ansatz exactly as defined in [[def-tgr-charged-liouville-data]]. Adopt whole-shell stationarity $\mathcal L_{F,q}f=0$ as the exchange criterion. This is a model assumption on every future mass-shell momentum, not an assertion that collisions drive a gas to this ansatz.

The two protocols are separate model choices. This postulate does not derive either protocol from gravity, assert a global electrostatic potential when no single-valued symmetry compensator exists, establish a Gibbs state or material realization, or identify finite entropy variables with kinetic fields without an explicit model assumption.

items.title: Conditional Tolman–Klein relation
items.physical_scope: Conditional redshift relation in either the stated connected charged kinetic model or a finite independent-cell entropy-exchange model; no universal chemical law, chemical reaction, hydrostatic equation of state, or non-exact global potential.
items.design_state: Authored draft for the reserved selected stationary thermal-equilibrium claim; exact hypotheses and source dispositions are recorded in batch-66 notes.
items.statement:
Use the selected stationary carrier of [[post-tgr-stationary-equilibrium]] and the declared exchange protocol of [[post-tgr-equilibrium-particle-exchange]]. The following two conclusions are conditional on their respective model inputs.

**Charged kinetic protocol.** Let $O$ be connected, let $\xi$ be the selected future timelike Killing field, and set $N_\xi=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$. For a species with $m>0$ and charge $q$, assume a global smooth potential symmetry $\mathcal L_\xi A=d\Lambda_\xi$ and define $\Phi_\xi=-c(\iota_\xi A-\Lambda_\xi)$ in volts. Suppose the smooth fields $T>0$ and $\mu$ define $\beta=u/(k_BT)$ and $\zeta=\mu/(k_BT)$, and the ansatz $f=\exp(\zeta+g(\beta,P))$ is stationary under the charged transport of [[def-tgr-charged-liouville-data]] at every future massive-shell momentum. Then there are constants $T_K>0$ and $\mu_K$ such that

$N_\xi T=T_K,\qquad \beta=\frac{\xi}{k_BT_K},\qquad N_\xi\mu+q\Phi_\xi=\mu_K.$

Here $\mu$ and $\mu_K$ use the same full-energy convention as the conserved generator, including rest energy when that generator includes it. The gauge-compensated potential reference may be shifted by $\Phi_\xi\mapsto\Phi_\xi+C$ only with $\mu_K\mapsto\mu_K+qC$.

**Finite-cell exchange protocol.** For $r\ge1$ finitely many independent cells with $C^1$ concave entropies $S_i(E_i,n_i)$, positive lapse values $N_i$, common charge $q$, and the supplied potential values $\Phi_i$, define $1/T_i=\partial_{E_i}S_i>0$ and $\mu_i/T_i=-\partial_{n_i}S_i$ at a supplied feasible interior point. If independent variations preserving $\sum_i(N_iE_i+q\Phi_i n_i)$ and $\sum_i n_i$ leave the total entropy stationary, then constants $T_K>0,\mu_K$ exist with

$N_iT_i=T_K,\qquad N_i\mu_i+q\Phi_i=\mu_K\quad(1\le i\le r).$

That stationary point is a global entropy maximum on the feasible set when the cell entropies are concave, and it is unique if they are strictly concave. No existence or boundary attainment is asserted. In either branch, $q=0$ gives the neutral relation $N\mu=\mu_K$ (or $N_i\mu_i=\mu_K$). The finite-cell symbols are not identified with the kinetic fields unless the model explicitly supplies that identification.

items.title: Defined classical Jüttner kinetic preparation
items.physical_scope: One massive classical species with prescribed positive density and temperature and a chosen observer congruence; an exactly normalized model preparation, not an assertion of collisional equilibration, material validity, or quantum statistics.
items.design_state: Authored draft for the reserved selected stationary thermal-equilibrium claim; exact hypotheses and source dispositions are recorded in batch-66 notes.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N_0)$ be the smooth time-oriented Lorentzian geometry of [[def-tgr-framework-units]], with signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and physical length coordinates $x^0=ct$. On an open region $O\subseteq M$, take a smooth observer congruence $u$ whose value at each event is a future unit timelike observer in the sense of [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]] and [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]. The congruence is a field of observer directions, not an adapted coordinate chart or a tetrad. Let $n:O\to(0,\infty)$ be a smooth proper number density in $\mathrm{m^{-3}}$ and $T:O\to(0,\infty)$ a smooth proper-temperature scalar in kelvins. These fields are prescribed model data.

Choose one species with rest mass $m>0$ in kilograms, put $M_*:=mc^2>0$ in joules, choose $k_B>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, and choose a reference action $h_{\rm ref}>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$. At an event $x\in O$, the future massive shell $\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}$ and its tetrad-independent measure $d\mu_{M_*}$ are those of [[def-tgr-future-mass-shell-measure]]. For each $P\in\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}$, define the positive observer-measured energy

$$E_u(P):=-g_x(P,u_x)>0,\qquad \alpha(x):=\frac{1}{k_BT(x)}.$$

In any future orthonormal tetrad whose time axis is $u_x$, write the spatial energy-momentum coordinates as $\mathbf p\in\mathbb R^3$, so $E_u(P)=\sqrt{M_*^2+|\mathbf p|^2}$ and $d^3\mathbf p=E_u(P)\,d\mu_{M_*}(P)$. The spatial mechanical momentum is $\mathbf p/c$; $\mathbf p$ itself is the spatial part of the energy four-vector $P$.

Define

$$Z_{M_*}(\alpha):=\frac{4\pi M_*^2}{\alpha}K_2(\alpha M_*),\qquad K_j(z):=\int_0^\infty e^{-z\cosh t}\cosh(jt)\,dt\quad(j=1,2).$$

and the observer-rest momentum probability law

$$d\nu_{u,x}(\mathbf p):=Z_{M_*}(\alpha(x))^{-1}e^{-\alpha(x)E_u(P)}\,d^3\mathbf p.$$

Set

$$\beta:=\frac{u}{k_BT},\qquad \zeta:=\log\!\left(\frac{n h_{\rm ref}^3c^3}{Z_{M_*}(\alpha)}\right),\qquad f(x,P):=e^{\zeta(x)+g_x(\beta(x),P)}.$$

Finally define the model number current and stress-energy tensor by the convergent shell moments

$$J^a(x):=(h_{\rm ref}^3c^3)^{-1}\int_{\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}}P^a f(x,P)\,d\mu_{M_*}(P),\qquad \mathsf T^{ab}(x):=(h_{\rm ref}^3c^3)^{-1}\int_{\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}}P^aP^b f(x,P)\,d\mu_{M_*}(P).$$

The mathematical suppliers [[thm-tgr-juttner-partition-and-moments]] and [[def-probability-measure]] give $0<Z_{M_*}<\infty$, show that $\nu_{u,x}$ has total mass one, and evaluate the current and stress moments:

$$J^a=nu^a,\qquad \mathsf T^{ab}=(\varepsilon+p)u^au^b+pg^{ab},\qquad \varepsilon=n\left(M_*\frac{K_1(\alpha M_*)}{K_2(\alpha M_*)}+\frac3\alpha\right),\quad p=\frac n\alpha=nk_BT.$$

Here $\varepsilon$ and $p$ are the exact moments of this one-species kinetic model. They are not automatically identified with an independently adopted material state function or stress tensor. The suppliers use the stated countable-choice strength $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ only; this definition adds no arbitrary-index choice principle. The scale $h_{\rm ref}$ is a declared phase-space unit convention, not Planck's constant or a measured parameter.

This is an exact classical model definition. It does not claim that an actual material realizes this distribution, that collisions drive it to equilibrium, that the full field $f$ solves a transport equation, or that any quantum-statistical or empirical law follows.

items.title: Schwarzschild supported thermal bath
items.physical_scope: Static test bath on the Schwarzschild exterior r>r_s, with asymptotic Killing-time normalization, exact lapse and acceleration, and a bounded weak-field expansion; no horizon or quantum-temperature claim.
items.design_state: Authored draft for the reserved selected stationary thermal-equilibrium claim; exact hypotheses and source dispositions are recorded in batch-66 notes.
items.statement:
Let $m_s>0$ be a source mass in kilograms, distinct from any kinetic particle mass, let $G_N>0$ be Newton's constant in $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, and let $c>0$ be the speed of light in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Set

$r_s:=\frac{2G_Nm_s}{c^2},\qquad f(r):=1-\frac{r_s}{r},\qquad r>r_s.$

In physical length coordinates $x^0=ct$, use the Schwarzschild exterior metric

$ds^2=-f(r)(dx^0)^2+f(r)^{-1}dr^2+r^2(d\theta^2+\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2),$

and select $\xi=\partial_{x^0}$ with the asymptotic normalization $N_\xi\to1$ as $r\to\infty$. The time orientation is chosen so $\xi$ is future-directed. Under the selected stationary-bath assumption, the local proper temperature satisfies

$T(r)=\frac{T_\infty}{\sqrt{1-r_s/r}},\qquad T_\infty:=T_K>0.$

The static observer congruence has outward covariant acceleration component $a_r=r_s/(2r^2f)$, contravariant component $a^r=r_s/(2r^2)$, and physical proper-acceleration magnitude

$c^2\sqrt{g_{ab}a^aa^b}=\frac{G_Nm_s}{r^2\sqrt{f(r)}}.$

For a fixed $z_0\in(0,1)$ and $0<r_s/r\le z_0$, the weak-field expansion has the explicit bound

$\left|\frac{T(r)}{T_\infty}-1-\frac{G_Nm_s}{c^2r}\right|\le\frac38(1-z_0)^{-5/2}\left(\frac{r_s}{r}\right)^2.$

This is a conditional calculation in the specified exterior model. At $r=r_s$, the chosen Killing field is null and the normalized stationary observers do not exist. The limiting divergence as $r\downarrow r_s$ is not a constructed horizon state, a Hawking temperature, or a claim that every observer measures an infinite temperature.

references.locator: Full 197-page PDF; Schwarzschild metric and static observer clock normalization, PDF pp. 144–155.

references.locator: Full 7-page PDF; static Killing-flow temperature relation and Schwarzschild/Reissner–Nordström context, PDF pp. 3 and 5–6.

items.title: Rindler and rigid rotating bath domains
items.physical_scope: Rindler right wedge and rigidly rotating Minkowski domain inside its light cylinder; arbitrary positive classical reference temperature; differential rotation and one-mode trace restrictions kept distinct.
items.design_state: Authored draft for the reserved selected stationary thermal-equilibrium claim; exact hypotheses and source dispositions are recorded in batch-66 notes.
items.statement:
**Rindler right wedge.** Let $a_0>0$ be an acceleration in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$, use coordinates $(x^0,x,y,z)$ with $x^0=ct$, and take the open domain $x>0$ with metric

$ds^2=-\left(\frac{a_0x}{c^2}\right)^2(dx^0)^2+dx^2+dy^2+dz^2.$

The selected Killing field $\xi_R=\partial_{x^0}$ has lapse $N_R=a_0x/c^2$ and observer acceleration $a_x=1/x$, so the physical proper-acceleration magnitude is $c^2/x$. The selected stationary-bath model gives

$T_R(x)=\frac{T_Kc^2}{a_0x}.$

At the reference point $x_{\rm ref}=c^2/a_0$, $N_R=1$ and $T_R=T_K$. Any $T_K>0$ is allowed by this classical geometric model; the metric and temperature relation do not select the Unruh value.

**Rigid rotation in Minkowski spacetime.** In cylindrical coordinates let

$ds^2=-(dx^0)^2+dr^2+r^2d\phi^2+dz^2,\qquad \xi_\Omega=\partial_{x^0}+\frac{\Omega}{c}\partial_\phi,$

where $\Omega$ is a constant angular velocity in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$. For $\Omega\ne0$, use the annular domain $0<r<c/|\Omega|$; for $\Omega=0$, $\xi_\Omega=\partial_{x^0}$ is timelike throughout Minkowski space. On the rotating domain,

$N_\Omega=\sqrt{1-\frac{\Omega^2r^2}{c^2}},\qquad T_\Omega(r)=\frac{T_K}{N_\Omega}.$

The radial acceleration component is $a_r=-\Omega^2r/[c^2(1-\Omega^2r^2/c^2)]$, directed inward, with physical magnitude $\gamma^2\Omega^2r$, where $\gamma=(1-\Omega^2r^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$. At the light cylinder $r=c/|\Omega|$, $\xi_\Omega$ becomes null and the normalized stationary observer does not exist. A differential-rotation field $\partial_{x^0}+[\Omega(r)/c]\partial_\phi$ is not Killing when $\Omega'(r)\ne0$: its metric Lie derivative has $(\mathcal L_\xi g)_{r\phi}=r^2\Omega'(r)/c$.

**One-mode trace check.** If an additional model specifies a single bosonic mode with lab Hamiltonian $H=\epsilon\mathcal N$ and angular momentum $J=\hbar j\mathcal N$, then its rotating generator is $H-\Omega J$. Its Gibbs trace is finite exactly when $\epsilon-\hbar j\Omega>0$. This is the separate one-mode spectral condition of [[prop-tgr-rotating-mode-gibbs-obstruction]]; it does not prove a continuum-field trace obstruction or describe every rotating equilibrium state.
